answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with endorsement staking: a new identity may not transact until K distinct, already-established agents publicly vouch for it, each staking reputation that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Attackers cannot just mint keys — they must corrupt real vouchers, making fake identities scarce and costly. Each endorsement is a marble token carrying a cryptographic cipher signature, and a tampered vote leaves a violet-stained audit trail anyone can verify on-chain, so identity farming becomes expensive and visible.
